fact_label: Eligible-nationality list -- EU/EEA freedom of movement (Directive 2004/38/EC)
value_raw: AT, BE, CY, CZ, DE, DK, EE, ES, FI, FR, GR, HR, HU, IE, IS, IT, LI, LT, LU, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SE, SI, SK
date: 2004-04-29 (Directive 2004/38/EC adopted; transposition deadline 2006-04-30; consolidated text current through amending Directive 2011/24/EU, in force 2011-06-16)
notes: Verified directly against Directive 2004/38/EC's consolidated text (EUR-Lex, CELEX:02004L0038-20110616, fetched directly 2026-07-21, primary-source-recheck) -- [specialist]-keyed, priority coverage build-out. Every other EU/EEA member-state nationality holds a treaty right of free movement and residence in Bulgaria under this Directive -- confirmed operative text: Art. 5 (no entry visa/formality for a Union citizen with valid ID/passport), Art. 6 (residence up to 3 months unconditional), Art. 7 (residence beyond 3 months conditional on worker/self-employed/sufficient-resources-plus-insurance/student/family-member status), Art. 8 (post-arrival registration is a formality, never a precondition). BG is excluded from this row's own membership list -- a Bulgarian national is already home, not a foreign national entering Bulgaria, not a foreign national needing this treaty right to enter/reside in Bulgaria. **Tier-shape judgment call, named plainly:** an early framing described this as a conservative-default-plus-conditional-relief shape; re-deriving from the Directive's own text directly, that reading doesn't hold -- `exempt` is the reader's actual, unconditional entry/short-stay tier regardless of whether Art. 7's conditions are ever met (Art. 6 carries no condition at all), and the note discloses an ADDITIONAL, better-secured right (indefinite residence) some readers can reach on top of it -- the same shape as Mexico's/Argentina's third-country-visa facilities, not the MX-SAE/CR-PT-biometric shape where the headline tier itself is the fallback a reader gets absent the condition. Checked directly against the Directive's own text before settling on this reading. **Switzerland named and left in debt, not rounded up:** Swiss nationals move under a separate 1999 EU-Switzerland Agreement on the Free Movement of Persons, not this Directive -- two primary-tier fetch attempts this sitting (eda.admin.ch, ec.europa.eu) both failed to resolve (403/404, the same gov-domain fetch-blocking pattern this project has hit before), so CH's own standing ships unverified and absent from this bloc tonight, owed as a follow-up primary-source-recheck rather than assumed symmetric. Sibling rows: ES/PT/CR/BG each carry their own independently-derived version of this same finding (this project's own inherited-claims discipline -- not copied across unverified).
document_conditional_note: Residence beyond three months requires meeting one of several conditions (Directive 2004/38/EC Art. 7): being a worker or self-employed, having sufficient resources plus comprehensive health insurance, being an enrolled student with resources and insurance, or being a qualifying family member of someone who meets one of those. This is an additional, better-secured right some readers can go on to claim -- it is never a condition on the entry/short-stay tier shown above, which is already unconditionally true for up to three months under Art. 6 ("without any conditions or any formalities other than the requirement to hold a valid identity card or passport"). A host state may ask for registration after arrival (Art. 8), but the Directive states plainly that holding a registration certificate "may under no circumstances be made a precondition for the exercise of a right" -- a formality, not a gate.
